goal: Look up canary-1 in CMDB to determine its host role, criticality, owner, and trust edges
what_to_summarize: Host role assigned by inventory
Criticality level (sandbox/dev/preprod/prod)
Owner or team responsible
Any declared trust_edges_out
Per-host users override if present

goal: Check for any successful sshd Accepted password/publickey auth on canary-1 in a wider window around the alert
what_to_summarize: Any sshd 'Accepted' events on canary-1 in the window 07:40-08:00Z
If found: username, source IP, auth method (password/publickey/gssapi), timestamp
Whether any success follows the failure burst (credential stuffing success pattern)
Also check for v2-sshd-success-after-failures alert hits on canary-1

params.query:
FROM .internal.alerts-security.alerts-default-*
| WHERE @timestamp >= "2026-07-25T07:40:00Z" AND @timestamp < "2026-07-25T08:00:00Z"
        AND kibana.alert.rule.rule_id == "v2-sshd-success-after-failures"
        AND host.name == "canary-1"
| STATS alerts     = COUNT(*),
        first_seen = MIN(@timestamp),
        last_seen  = MAX(@timestamp)
        BY rule     = kibana.alert.rule.name,
           rule_id  = kibana.alert.rule.rule_id,
           severity = kibana.alert.severity,
           host.name
| SORT alerts DESC

FROM logs-system.auth-*
| WHERE @timestamp >= "2026-07-25T07:40:00Z" AND @timestamp < "2026-07-25T08:00:00Z"
        AND host.name == "canary-1"
        AND event.outcome IS NOT NULL
| STATS accepted   = COUNT(*) WHERE event.outcome == "success",
        failed     = COUNT(*) WHERE event.outcome == "failure",
        first_seen = MIN(@timestamp),
        last_seen  = MAX(@timestamp)
        BY auth_method = CASE(message LIKE "*publickey*", "publickey",
                              message LIKE "*password*",  "password", "other"),
           source.ip, user.name
| SORT accepted DESC, failed DESC

goal: Extract raw sshd Failed password events on canary-1 in the alert window to identify source IPs, targeted usernames, and failure pattern
what_to_summarize: Distinct source IPs in Failed password messages
Distinct usernames targeted in Failed password messages
Timing pattern: are failures evenly spaced (scanner) or rapid-fire (brute-force)?
Sample raw message lines showing the OpenSSH format
Total count of Failed password events in the window

params.query:
FROM logs-system.auth-*
| WHERE @timestamp >= "2026-07-25T07:48:37.065Z" AND @timestamp < "2026-07-25T07:45:35.000Z"
        AND host.name == "canary-1"
        AND event.outcome == "failure"
| STATS failed_count = COUNT(*),
        first_seen = MIN(@timestamp),
        last_seen = MAX(@timestamp),
        sample_message = MAX(message)
        BY source.ip, user.name
| SORT failed_count DESC, source.ip ASC
| LIMIT 1000

FROM logs-system.auth-*
| WHERE @timestamp >= "2026-07-25T07:48:37.065Z" AND @timestamp < "2026-07-25T07:45:35.000Z"
        AND host.name == "canary-1"
        AND event.outcome == "failure"
| STATS failed_count = COUNT(*),
        first_seen = MIN(@timestamp),
        last_seen = MAX(@timestamp),
        sample_message = MAX(message)
        BY source.ip, user.name, message
| SORT failed_count DESC
| LIMIT 10

FROM logs-system.auth-*
| WHERE @timestamp >= "2026-07-25T07:48:37.065Z" AND @timestamp < "2026-07-25T07:45:35.000Z"
        AND host.name == "canary-1"
        AND event.outcome == "failure"
| STATS failed_per_minute = COUNT(*),
        first_in_minute = MIN(@timestamp),
        last_in_minute = MAX(@timestamp)
        BY minute = DATE_TRUNC(1 minute, @timestamp)
| SORT minute ASC
| LIMIT 1000

FROM logs-system.auth-*
| WHERE @timestamp >= "2026-07-25T07:48:37.065Z" AND @timestamp < "2026-07-25T07:45:35.000Z"
        AND host.name == "canary-1"
        AND event.outcome == "failure"
| STATS total_failed = COUNT(*),
        distinct_src_ips = COUNT_DISTINCT(source.ip),
        distinct_users = COUNT_DISTINCT(user.name),
        first_seen = MIN(@timestamp),
        last_seen = MAX(@timestamp)
| LIMIT 1

goal: Identify what host/container is at IP 172.18.0.15 by searching all log streams for this IP — look for host.name associations, Zeek SSH client versions, and any other identifying information
what_to_summarize: Any log stream where 172.18.0.15 appears as source.ip or destination.ip
Zeek logs-zeek.ssh-* records showing SSH client version from 172.18.0.15
Zeek logs-zeek.connection-* records involving 172.18.0.15
Any host.name associated with 172.18.0.15 in any log stream
What other services/ports 172.18.0.15 is connecting to

params.query:
FROM logs-zeek.ssh-*
| WHERE source.ip == "172.18.0.15" OR destination.ip == "172.18.0.15"
| STATS events = COUNT(*), first_seen = MIN(@timestamp), last_seen = MAX(@timestamp) BY source.ip, destination.ip, ssh.client, ssh.server
| SORT events DESC
| LIMIT 1000

FROM logs-zeek.connection-*
| WHERE source.ip == "172.18.0.15" OR destination.ip == "172.18.0.15"
| STATS conns = COUNT(*), bytes_out = SUM(source.bytes), bytes_in = SUM(destination.bytes), dest_ips = COUNT_DISTINCT(destination.ip), first_seen = MIN(@timestamp), last_seen = MAX(@timestamp) BY destination.ip, destination.port
| SORT conns DESC
| LIMIT 1000

FROM logs-*
| WHERE source.ip == "172.18.0.15" OR client.ip == "172.18.0.15" OR host.ip == "172.18.0.15" OR destination.ip == "172.18.0.15"
| STATS events = COUNT(*), first_seen = MIN(@timestamp), last_seen = MAX(@timestamp) BY host.name, data_stream.dataset
| SORT events DESC
| LIMIT 1000

FROM logs-zeek.ssh-*
| WHERE source.ip == "172.18.0.15" OR destination.ip == "172.18.0.15"
| LIMIT 5

FROM logs-zeek.ssh-*
| WHERE source.ip == "172.18.0.15"
| STATS events = COUNT(*), first_seen = MIN(@timestamp), last_seen = MAX(@timestamp) BY zeek.ssh.client, destination.ip
| SORT events DESC
| LIMIT 1000

FROM logs-zeek.ssh-*
| WHERE source.ip == "172.18.0.15" OR destination.ip == "172.18.0.15"
| STATS events = COUNT(*), first_seen = MIN(@timestamp), last_seen = MAX(@timestamp) BY source.ip, destination.ip, zeek.ssh.client, zeek.ssh.server
| SORT events DESC
| LIMIT 1000
